value.content: {"id": "portswigger_business_logic", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "business_logic", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: Business Logic Vulnerabilities", "name": "Business Logic & State Machine Subversion Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-840", "owasp_category": "A04:2021 - Insecure Design", "signals": ["negative_numeric_quantities", "integer_overflow_wrapping", "multi_step_workflow_skipping", "reusable_one_time_coupon", "client_side_price_tampering", "inconsistent_unit_pricing"], "verification_strategy": "Analyze multi-step workflows (e.g. cart -> checkout -> payment -> confirmation) for step skipping. Test numerical boundary conditions including negative values, zero, fractional inputs, and large numbers susceptible to 32-bit integer truncation or rounding errors. Test concurrent coupon redemption.", "evidence_requirements": ["workflow_step_skipped_proof", "negative_total_transaction", "unauthorized_discount_calculation"], "tools": [{"tool": "TemporalLogicVerifier (HunterAI)", "cmd": "TemporalLogicVerifier.audit_workflow_transitions(trace)", "desc": "Applies Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) to verify required state machine steps"}, {"tool": "BurpAgent (Workflow Replay)", "cmd": "BurpAgent.tamper_workflow_params(step_data)", "desc": "Systematically tests parameter tampering across checkout workflows"}], "remediation": "Enforce all business logic rules strictly on the server side. Enforce monotonic progression through multi-step transactions using server-side session state. Validate numerical quantities for positive integer constraints.", "description": "PortSwigger Business Logic vulnerabilities cover excessive trust in client-side controls, negative quantity cart manipulation, bypassing authentication flow via status step skipping, integer truncation in high-value transactions, and infinite money logic."}
